items.title: Avery "Kid" Howard Interview, 1961-05-22
items.q: The interviewee (Kid Howard) does not mention Louis Armstrong in the provided transcript; the mention is made by the Interviewer.

ctx.x: Well that's very hard to say because George was there for about I think eight or ten days in total, you know. And that was full, the club was full, very, every night. And Stan was there for almost a year. And the first eight days was very full naturally as it would be. And then it balanced out so that it was Friday, Saturday and Sunday was very full. And Copenhagen is a city of about a million people or something like that. And there's just a natural demand for jazz. And they stayed so long. Sure should have…
So then George Louis Armstrong is about as well as anybody in Europe then, roughly.

I would say so. I mean Louis Armstrong is, I mean Louis Armstrong takes in a lot of people that are not particularly interested in jazz but because of the outstanding amount of publicity he gets and because he also plays humorous versions of numbers that are well known to a lot of old timers because you might realize that in Europe it's the young people that go for jazz, college students and all the young boys and girls. And Louis Armstrong was just the first band to come over and make a success out of jazz in…
